questions.stemHtml: Post-mortem lividity shown in the image is due to ………Poisoning
questions.solutionHtml:
Carbon monoxide
  • In a case of CO poisoning, the cherry-red colouration of the skin, mucous membranes, conjunctivae, nail beds, areas of hypostasis, blood, tissues and internal organs are seen in 15 to 20% of cases only.
  • The cherry-red discolouration changes to dark green, then to brown with the onset of decomposition.
  • The blood is fluid, hyperaemia is general and serous effusions are common.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 34th Edition, Page Number: 24 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 18

questions.stem: Two friends were fighting as practice. However, as one punched the other over his neck, the other collapsed to the ground. Death following a ‘commando punch’ is due:

options.label: D
options.text: Fracture dislocation of the cervical spine

questions.solutionHtml:
Reflex cardiac inhibition
  • In "commando punch", the edge of the hand is brought forcibly across the side of the neck or the front of the larynx.
  • Blows directly to the larynx, indirectly stimulates the sinus region, or the laryngeal sensory nerve endings and may trigger the cardio-inhibitory reflex.



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 34th Edition, Page Number: 603 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 495

questions.stem: A person was found unconscious in a burning building. He had no burns. Which of the following gas has systemic toxicity without irritation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Carbon monoxide
  • Carbon monoxide is a colourless, tasteless, non-irritative gas which is produced due to the incomplete combustion of carbon.
  • Victims may not notice anything, except a headache, until they lapse into a coma and die.
  • The effects of CO are simply those of suboxia.
  • As most deaths are relatively rapid, blisters are rare. 



KSN Reddy Essential Textbook of Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, 34th Edition, Page Number: 603 & 35th Edition, Page Number: 495
